Wimbledon.text: on the conditions: "As it got darker I had the feeling that dew started to fall. The court became terribly slippery and we both slipped a couple of times. During a match so many factors come together — first sunshine, then you play in the shade, the wind blows, then the roof closes and it starts to get slippery. It is really demanding to adapt to all these changes instantly."

after beating Tien: "It was a tough match. There were breaks of serve going both ways, and that's tennis. On a court like this the conditions are slow, so you can't rely too much on your serve. That's why it became such a physical match, and fortunately I was the stronger player." On the match: "At the start of the second set my opponent needed a medical timeout. I could see she was physically struggling, and I felt I had to put her under even more pressure and finish the set strongly." On the first set: "The first set lasted 70 minutes and I felt it slipped away from me. I had more chances, more break points, and I was leading in the tie-break. I felt I was playing well, serving well, hitting the ball well and moving well, so I knew I just had to keep going."
WIMBLEDON: "Here (Wimbledon) the grass is a bit longer, there (Queen's) it's a bit shorter," said F. Cerundolo.

WIMBLEDON: "I think the grass at Wimbledon is very different from what it was at the warm-up tournaments," said Cobolli. "The court here is noticeably slower, and I think that could work in my favor and help me show my best tennis. Last year I managed to perform well here, and now I hope to at least match that result, and maybe even surpass it. The transition to grass is never easy, but I feel like I'm adapting better to it every day."

WIMBLEDON: "It is true that the surfaces are different," said Fonseca. "Halle is faster, Eastbourne a bit slower, and here the grass is slower. You have to adapt to each tournament, but I always look forward to Wimbledon."

after beating De Minaur: "It wasn’t a great start for me, he broke my serve three times in the first set. It was very windy and swirly conditions, and he was managing them better from the back of the court. There was a lot of cat and mouse, a lot of slices. He’s one of the quickest, and on the grass, where the ball doesn’t bounce, he can expose a lot of weaknesses. He’s really tough to play on this surface. I’m just happy I could hang in there. There were a lot of challenging moments for me. I didn’t feel the ball so well, but I was trying to mix it up and find my game, and then in the end I found my forehand." On grabbing his stomach a couple of times: "It was all good. I was just trying to manage the breathing."
WIMBLEDON: "This year has been a bit different, different tennis at Wimbledon with a different feel," said Alcaraz. "I see everything a bit slower, the balls slower, a different sensation."

WIMBLEDON: "I think it's the same as in previous years," said De Minaur. "Three, four, five years, it has always been the same kind of speed. It's slower, but it's something we all know and are accustomed to. Yes, if I had to compare it to Queen's, Queen's is always much faster than Wimbledon. You have a lot more time to adjust. Yes, it's about finding ways to use it to your advantage."

on the pace of the courts at Wimbledon: "I think the speed is pretty solid. One thing I've noticed this year, and I hadn't realized in previous years with all the tournaments I've played, is that it feels slower the more you play. It plays faster when it's newer. Last year, when I was in the quarterfinals, I felt it was very slow."

WIMBLEDON - Davidovich Fokina: "The only thing is that, with the heat, everything is a lot slower than in other years. The ball gets very heavy and it's slow compared to Eastbourne, for example." Misolic: "The grass is finer and a bit slower [than Roehampton]." Medvedev: "...the court was a little different. It was a little slower because of the heat."
on the difference between the grass at Roehampton and the grass at Wimbledon: "For me, it's completely different here: much better, the grass is finer and a bit slower."
WIMBLEDON, Centre Court with the roof closed: “For whatever reason, it feels much slower,” Medvedev said. “It’s a really slow bounce. I need to get used to it.”
WIMBLEDON: "It was slower here compared to the tournaments before on grass," said Barrere, who played in Eastbourne last week.

WIMBLEDON: "The court is a bit slower at the beginning of the tournament, and because the ball is bouncing lower, certain shots work much better... dropshots, slice," said Murray. "As the tournament goes on, it starts to play a little more like hard court. At the other majors, you don't get such a change in the conditions as the tournament goes on."
WIMBLEDON: "I thought Roehampton was a little faster," said Marterer. "It's a little slower here, probably because the grass is still quite high. It slows the ball a little."
WIMBLEDON: "...but in general the ball bounces very little this year, it seems to me that the grass is higher, because many balls tend to stop," said Musetti.
WIMBLEDON: "The courts are very green and very lush," said Norrie. "The balls are staying really low."

WIMBLEDON: "I would say muddy and humid," Auger-Aliassime said. "The back of the court on one side, the back right was literally mud. So that can be tricky for sure. You’re careful with your movement, try to be stable and always on my toes."

on the conditions and the match: "Today, however, the conditions were completely different. They were much easier for me and I think it showed, it was simpler for me to develop my game. The ball was bouncing a bit higher and I could attack more easily, but I reacted too late. Unfortunately the first two sets didn't go my way. When you play against a player like Sascha, who has so much confidence and who, in my opinion, is playing the best tennis of his career on grass, losing the first two sets is simply not enough if you want to win the match."

Hamburg.text: on the heavy conditions with the roof closed: "Of course the conditions were different — heavier ball, heavier court. But it’s the same for everyone. When you come to Germany, you know this can happen: sun, rain, sun, rain — all day like this." On reaching the semifinals in Hamburg again: "I’m happy to be back in the semifinals in Hamburg. It’s what I needed. I missed this type of match — the ones where I suffer but somehow win in the end. They give me a lot of confidence."
On Hamburg: "It's slower here, always raining. It's much slower than Rome."

HAMBURG: "It’s a bit slower here than other tournaments, but I like slower conditions," said F. Cerundolo. "I actually like both types. I played my whole life in Buenos Aires where it’s super slow, so it’s nothing new for me. But I also played well in Madrid, where it’s super fast."
HAMBURG: "I think it’s slower this year because of the cooler weather," said Darderi. "Maybe I need to improve my serve and attack more because the court is slower."
HAMBURG: "It was definitely slow under the roof and the ball was staying low, but I think it’s a great place for me to keep developing my clay-court tennis," said Shelton.

Madrid.text: MADRID: "The inside courts are a little bit slower," said F. Cerundolo. "They have more of a roof, they're in shade almost the whole day. Outside they're always with sun. It's totally different. The outside ones are faster, slippery and smaller. More like faster points, more free points outside than inside. Inside you have to play more rallies."

on playing in Madrid specifically: "When I'm in the zone, I probably prefer a tiny bit not exactly slower clay courts but not altitude. When I was playing unreal in Rome or Roland Garros, I could play better than here. But here if you serve well you have your chances. I do know that if I manage to play well here in Madrid on this surface with this altitude, I could maybe do something."
. Madrid is at high altitude, so the clay is faster and the bounce is higher

on the conditions in Madrid: "The conditions in Madrid suit me well, there is a little bit of altitude and the ball bounces higher. I am a player who makes the ball bounce quite a lot, and against a player like him that works in my favour, because I can make it feel like we are playing on clay. I am feeling very good and I hope to continue like this."

on what game style works best in Madrid: "If you serve well it's very effective. You have to play with topspin. If you play flat it might fly on you a little bit. All players that serve well have a better chance of going deep and doing some damage. I need to take care of that part of my game and if I do, then I can put pressure on some return games and have fun with that." On committing fully to every shot in the altitude: "It feels like on other conditions, sometimes you kind of hit half a shot, so to speak, like you don't fully finish the shot, and the ball was still going to court. Here it's very important to once you have your feet set up to really go through every shot and finish every shot and then recover for the next one. It's true on every surface and every condition, but I think even more so here."

MADRID: "The court is a bit slippery," said Sinner. "It is harder to move on it. The ball flies a bit faster. The speed of the game depends on the position of the sun. I practiced on the first day, it was evening, so everything is a bit different. When someone serves very well, it is not easy to return. Yes, this is a very unique court. It is very different from Rome and Paris. I think this is a separate tournament on clay courts."

on the conditions in Madrid: "The way I feel here is that normally with the way the ball bounces in the altitude, the thing that's under the clay is solid concrete. So whenever whoever plays a good kick serve, you are on the fence actually. The conditions here are more like if you are playing on a hardcourt because you can hold your serve in a much easier way. If you put a good serve, it's a good serve done. And on the return, a good return pays off. If you really go for it, you can play a little bit more from the baseline."
MADRID: "With the altitude, it’s tougher to control the ball and it plays even faster than Munich," said Shelton. "Some parts of my game can be really effective here and difficult to deal with."

on Madrid: "I have never played well here. I have not won a match here yet, but I think this year it will happen. I just have a few adjustments to find and it will work out. I come with a very positive mindset and we will see what happens." On the conditions: "The ball flies more at altitude, it escapes a little more and sometimes you miss shots that you are not used to missing. Either you decide to increase the tension of your racket, or you find another way to put the ball in the court. The goal is to control the ball."
MADRID: "The Madrid surface? I think it helps my game, it's a bit faster and it certainly helps my serve too," said Hurkacz.
MADRID: "I have never played very well here," said Sinner. "It's very particular, you play at altitude. It can be windy, it's very hard to play. It's one of the most difficult challenges for me."
Here it’s super fast and really suits the big servers, but I’ve beaten some good guys.

on the surface differences in Madrid: "Yes. Slippery. Although, by the way, I wouldn’t say so. On the third court, the clay itself is wetter, but at the same time, for example, today I felt a couple of times that when I was returning, I was slipping a little and it was harder to start, even on these courts. But, of course, there are differences."

on the Madrid court: "The court was unplayable today, it felt like an ice rink when I tried to slide. I had never felt something like this on a clay court. It is a different kind of clay from what is usually used, and I have a lot of experience on this surface, so it is frustrating to play like this."
I love playing on clay as it’s the surface I grew up playing. Since we’re playing at altitude I wanted to focus on my serve and play aggressive.

The conditions definitely help here. Madrid is way faster than the other clay court Masters 1000’s. We basically play indoors which makes it faster. I have no disrespect toward clay but sometimes when you play outdoor it’s a bit rough and rusty. Playing indoors on clay is much more consistent and it’s amazing.
I held my serve until the end which is especially important here in Madrid as conditions are quicker and it’s tougher to return

The conditions here in Madrid are usually quite fast, as there is a bit of altitude and the balls fly very fast through the air, but as people can see, it's been a little cold the last few days. So the balls aren't as fast as they usually are, which means maybe we're not hitting as fast. I have room to hit the ball a little better."

on Madrid: "It is not easy for me to play in Madrid because it is a very peculiar clay court, being faster and even a bit similar to hard courts. If I play on clay, I prefer typical conditions of that surface to make the required changes in my game. In the third set today I played with the confidence that I had in Rome last year, dominating the game."
On Madrid: “There’s a bit of altitude so it flies off the racquet a bit more. It takes some adjusting to.”

on Madrid: “The altitude is good for me. I’ve played in Madrid since I was little and I’m very comfortable. The altitude benefits my game and the energy of the fans really spurs me on." On playing Seyboth Wild: "He’s a very good player, with a lot of shots. Today he beat Musetti and he’s on a roll. I’ve seen him several times and I think his level is very high."

MADRID: “It is an altitude very similar to Chile," said Baez. "It can be a little drier. It is a good surface and good conditions to play. I see the altitude as what it is, I can't control it and you have to learn to play in these conditions."

on the conditions in Madrid: "I played on the center court yet this year, but I remember from previous years that the center court was a little slower. However, they are now telling me that they are the same as the outside ones, so I don't know exactly."

on Madrid: "I was able to just come out of tennis a little bit and then continue my preparation for Madrid. It’s not always easy to play here because of the altitude. I’m trying to adapt and prepare my next match. It’s time to fix some small things, make small adjustments and try to play better. Because of the altitude, maybe I can play better in Madrid than in other clay court tournaments. On clay, the toughest thing for me is the movement. I like to move on hard courts and run in front of the ball in long rallies, but on clay that’s not the case. I’m still trying to learn to slide right because I lose five seconds after every shot. But every year is a new opportunity, this year is another one and I’m gonna try to just play my best. Even on clay when I play well I feel capable of beating great guys, playing good tennis and going far in tournaments, like in Monte-Carlo this year."
"It’s fast here, the balls are fast in the altitude

on the conditions in Madrid: ”Of course, here we’re dealing with a little bit of altitude, which is a different scenario than Barcelona. I’m getting adjusted to that. It’s something that I’ve done pretty well in the past few years. I like the altitude, I think it’s good for my game. I see that as a small advantage.”
. In Madrid the conditions are always difficult. With the altitude, the ball bounces high
MADRID: "It’s a perfect combination — slow clay gives me time, but the altitude makes it faster, which suits my game," said Blockx.
